correctness.rationale: Smooth Birkhoff orthogonality gives x=(t,1)/(1+t^4)^(1/4), y=±(1,-t³)/(1+t^12)^(1/4), 0<=t<=1. Directly expanded the two branch products; the stated exact factorization shows the positive branch dominates for 0<t<1. The constrained derivative along (1+t^12)r^4=1+t^4 has a resultant proportional to the displayed palindromic degree-14 Q(t^4). Inspected exact SymPy verifying script checking this identity and Sturm root counts; independently computed Q roots in (0,1) near 0.002416998 and 0.825586362 and optimized both branches, obtaining t*=0.9532144723 and T=2.070379018225525. Only the large root is compatible with the positive constrained derivative; endpoint values are lower. Numerical computation is corroboration, while exact resultant/root isolation is the proof.
